name: Carve
describe: Explosions carve smooth craters in the terrain world; the host keeps the ground the same everywhere
examples: explosions blow smooth craters in the ground

fromProjectile.description: Carve where the projectile mechanic's shots end, when they have a splash (splashRadius > 0)

radius.description: Crater radius in metres (0: the shot's splash radius times scale)

scale.description: Crater radius per metre of the shot's splash radius

keep.description: Keep the craters from one round to the next (false: every round starts on the ground as it was made)

debris.description: Lumps of ground thrown out of each crater

blastFx.description: A vfx preset (kit/vfx: impact-flash, spark-burst, ...) at the heart of each blast; unset: none

dustFx.description: A vfx preset (kit/vfx: smoke-puff, dust-kick, ...) rising from each crater; unset: none

splashFx.description: A vfx preset (kit/vfx: smoke-puff, ...) where a blast lands in the sea and carves nothing; unset: none

splashSound.description: A sound id played where a blast lands in the sea; unset: none

sound.description: A sound id (assets.json → sounds) played at each crater; unset: none

shake.description: Camera shake at a blast next to the camera (m)

events.name: onCarve
events.args: { op: 'carve' | 'add', at: {x, y, z}, r, normal, live, by }
events.when: the ground changed here (live: false while a late copy catches up)

host.how: the host makes every edit and numbers it; every copy applies them in order on the same generated ground; a copy missing some asks the host for them

fields.r: the host's round count (a new round starts the ground again)
fields.n: how many edits the host has made this round

worlds.why: it edits the smooth terrain's field (config/world.json template "terrain")

bots: no bot code (bots fire the projectile; the craters come by themselves)

lines: With the projectile mechanic every shot with a splash (splashRadius > 0) carves where it ends by itself (fromProjectile); otherwise the host calls carve.carve({ x, y, z }, r).
Players fall when the ground under them goes, and into the sea past the land: the rules decide what the sea does (world.seaLevel).

stub.worked: carve.onCarve(c => { if (c.live) ctx.audio.play('explosion-small', { at: c.at, optional: true }); });
traps: carve.carve and carve.add change the ground on the host only: keep them under if (ctx.host)

signs: checked: gate C (measure 15) judges its sign of life (sample and judge in the implementation)
